newsitem.title: LIBERIA: Peacekeepers with tanks move on Liberian rebels.
newsitem.headline: Peacekeepers with tanks move on Liberian rebels.

text.p: Hundreds of African peacekeepers backed by tanks headed for western Liberia on Wednesday to clear out rebels blocking highways to international relief workers, witnesses said.
Troops of the Nigerian-led ECOMOG peacekeeping force in 16 trucks sang war songs and waved their weapons as they crossed the Po River bridge outside Monrovia.

Wednesday was the deadline given by ECOMOG commander General Victor Malu for guerrillas of General Roosevelt Johnson's ULIMO-J militia to dismantle roadblocks in the Grand Cape Mount and Bomi counties.
"We have ordered our troops to return fire if shot at first," Malu told Brtish Broadcasting Corporation radio.
"Knowing the faction we are dealing with we'll take no chances in Cape Mount and Tubmanburg."

Fighting between ECOMOG and ULIMO-J in the area last December and January was followed by militia warfare in Monrovia in April and May that derailed a 1995 accord on ending nearly seven years of civil war in Liberia.
An ECOMOG spokesman said the troops would split into two and simultaneously head for Cape Mount to the west and the ULIMO-J stronghold town of Tubmanburg.
"We do not expect resistance, but if that happens it would be unfortunate," spokesman Major Patrick Okoh told Reuters.
A West African summit in Nigeria last August pressured Liberia's squabbling warlords to sign a new accord providing for disarmament of 60,000 guerrillas and elections by May next year.
Despite symbolic gestures and promises of disarmament, the process has yet to take off in earnest as ECOMOG says it is waiting for troop reinforcements from regional states.
Militia clashes have meanwhile broken out in parts of the country, notably in the west where aid workers have been prevented from distributing food aid to starving people.
More than 150,000 people have died in the conflict in Liberia, which was founded by freed American slaves in 1847 as Africa's first independent republic.
The U.S. military helped evacuate foreigners at the height of the fighting in Monrovia in April and May and marines backed by warships offshore helped protect the American embassy.
